exposure: Surgeon report of surgical site infection (SSI)
Patient self-report of surgical site infection (SSI)
cohort: The study included 2853 surgical procedures performed on patients across four hospitals within one private health-care system.
finding: The surgeon-reported SSI rate was significantly lower (2.4%) compared with the patient self-report rate (4.3%), indicating that patient report is a more sensitive method for detecting SSIs.
mod_finding: Disagreements between surgeon and patient reports of SSI were more likely in C-sections (22.7% reported by patients vs. 17.7% by surgeons).
